column1: # Checks that need their own command line. Columns (tab separated): check, kind, rows, spec.
#   kind  device: runs inside container A from ~/ds (python3 ..., sudo password on stdin from HP_SUDO_PASS)
#         console: <script in console/scripts> <page path> [globals JSON], on the live console (ORIGIN, STATE, PW_CHROMIUM, NODE_PATH)
#         cmd: a shell command on the machine running this runner
#   rows  comma list of row ids, or @script.py for every row whose Linux evidence names that script; EXTRA for the final extras

#   spec  placeholders {build} {version} (the installed version) {previous} {origin} {state} {host} {self} {peer} (machine names of containers a and b) {ct_a} {ct_b} {ct_user} {ct_uid} (container user and uid)
#         local-access and private-access-permission run from this host through tools/device-smoke/ctssh/ssh (their ssh destinations are
#         containers): F9_CONTROLLER F9_TARGET F9_OWNER F9_OWNER_ALIAS F9_ACCESSOR F9_TEAM are set by final_recheck.py from its own
#         containers and the fixtures' team (the teammate's machine is container D of the second throwaway account)
# A script not listed here is not run by the final re-check: `final_recheck.py inventory` lists the [x] rows that depend on it.
# env-vault-lifecycle initialises the fresh account's vault and leaves it unlocked: it runs before command-rows (C143/C144 fail on a locked vault)
# env-ssh-hook and env-vscode-remote ssh from container A to its own sshd (final_self_ssh.sh); local-access runs inside A against B (installs iptables for its relay-path phase)

column4: umask 077; head -c 24 /dev/urandom | base64 > ~/vault-password; head -c 24 /dev/urandom | base64 > ~/vault-recovery; python3 env_vault_lifecycle.py ~/vault-password ~/vault-recovery; code=$?; rm -f ~/vault-password ~/vault-recovery; exit $code

column1: # Tunnel command rows: runner environment SMOKE_SERVER_VERSION, SMOKE_DNS_ZONE, FINAL_FIXTURES_URL and FINAL_FIXTURES_TOKEN_FILE (local 0600 file; the runner sets them from FINAL_FIXTURES_URL/FINAL_FIXTURES_TOKEN).
# Each suite invocation gets its own temporary token copy; the suite removes it. C126 needs a ready private TCP route on B,
# identified by runner environment SMOKE_PRIVATE_TUNNEL_ID and SMOKE_PRIVATE_ROUTE_ID; the fixture owner cleans it up.

column1: # Config command checks require signed-in account cleanup authority and no active config assignment; sudo password uses runner stdin.
# Second-account checks. They need the member account's fixtures (env on the runner): SMOKE_MEMBER_SSH (ssh alias of a container paired to the
# member account, default laneh-s5hm), SMOKE_CT_A_SSH (ssh alias of container a, default laneh-s5ha), SMOKE_OWNER_MACHINE_ID (container a's
# machine id) and SMOKE_MEMBER_MACHINE_ID (the member container's; the check REMOVES it, so create it for this run only).
# The suspension section is skipped: it writes to the server database.
# F3-04: an idle session survives 8 hours. Run session-idle-start first thing, session-idle-verify at least 8 h later (final_recheck.py run --only
# session-idle-verify); the start is a background job of the final run, not a blocking step.
# Linux scripts the final re-check does not run, and why (a row citing only these shows NO CHECK in `inventory`):
#   account_inventory.py, machine_lifecycle.py revoke: revoke removes the peer machine; the other machine_lifecycle checks run above
#   config_team_default.py: needs a GitHub config repository connected to the account and a team the account administers
#   deploy.py, device_install.py: harness tools that build and install onto devices, not checks

#   private_access_permission.py: needs a second team-member account with a machine and a paid team the owner administers; it runs with F9_OWNER F9_OWNER_ALIAS F9_ACCESSOR F9_TEAM from the environment, never on the run's fresh account

#   official_update.py, update_continuity.py, update_failures.py, update_survival.py: need an official install, a second build and a wrong-platform binary; run by the update step of the final re-check
#   session_idle.py: needs an 8 hour idle between its start and verify phases
#   session_share_cross.py, team_two_account.py, team_machines.py, team_business.py: need two accounts (owner and team member), some also a server database or S3 target

column4: for c in rename settings availability capabilities; do python3 machine_lifecycle.py $c || exit 1; done
! test -e server/internal/sync && ! test -e cli/internal/controlsync && ! grep -rIl --include=*.go -e internal/controlsync -e 'paperboat/server/internal/sync"' server cli shared tunnel relay helper

cd tools/device-smoke && python3 machine_tags.py --owner-cmd 'ssh {host} docker exec -i -u {ct_user} -e HOME=/home/{ct_user} -e XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/{ct_uid} {ct_a}' --target {peer} --pb /home/{ct_user}/.local/bin/pb

column1: # Managed SSH (Lane I). device checks run in container A and dial {peer}, the machine with sshd; ssh-trust-host
# rotates {ct_b}'s ed25519 host key as root, so {ct_b} must be the container of {peer}. ssh-long holds one hour.
# Login approval and the destructive pairing checks. auth-lifecycle signs container A out and back in, approving the login link
# in headless Chromium with the run's account ({state}). destructive makes its own throwaway container from the build container A
# runs, paired to the same account, runs uninstall/re-pair/interrupted setup/reset there, then revokes and removes it.

column4: ssh {host} 'docker exec {ct_a} cat /home/{ct_user}/.local/bin/pb > /tmp/final-pb-{version}' && python3 tools/device-smoke/destructive_suite.py {host} /tmp/final-pb-{version} {version} final-destr-{version}; c=$?; ssh {host} 'rm -f /tmp/final-pb-{version}'; exit $c
